subject: Nariway Signals - 2026-08-14
html:
Nariway Signals — 2026-08-14

See this soon (time-sensitive)

  • Christie's Medaugh Hiroshige preview dates are now published: public preview Sept 11–14, sale Sept 15, 2026, at Christie's, 20 Rockefeller Plaza. Four weeks out — put it on the calendar now. Source
  • Heckerling Institute (Jan 11–15, 2027) early registration closes Sept 30, 2026 ($1,200 vs. $1,250 regular) — the deadline to actually decide on the year's biggest travel commitment.

Cases

  • Deutsche Bank is closing PalaisPopulaire, its dedicated Berlin exhibition house for the Deutsche Bank Collection (~55,000 works), at the end of 2026 — stepping back from a standalone public building to a rotating-loan model with partner institutions, while keeping its "Artist of the Year" prize alive in a new roving format from 2027. The clean corporate mirror of CAM Raleigh (logged 2026-08-13): the building, not the collection or the commitment, was what stopped paying for itself. Source
  • Muzej Lah opens at Lake Bled, Slovenia, this summer — Igor and Mojca Lah's 800+-work, three-decade collection (Kiefer, Beuys, the Kabakovs, Kentridge, Mušič, NSK) goes public for the first time in a purpose-built David Chipperfield museum. The small/regional/distinctive, living-founder, new-region pattern the filter favors. Source

Partners

  • Matthew F. Erskine, T&E attorney (Erskine & Erskine, Worcester MA) specializing in art and other illiquid assets, and a long-running Forbes columnist on exactly Nariway's terrain. His Aug 4, 2026 piece lays out Private Operating Foundations as a private-museum vehicle almost verbatim to Nariway's own framing. Source
  • Betsy Bickar, Head of Art Advisory at Citi Wealth. Not a referral lead — a landscape marker for the bank-advisory alternative to Nariway's independent model. Source

Events register housekeeping

  • Fondation Beyeler's Zumthor expansion opens in phases: portions of the new campus open from autumn 2026, full ensemble complete January 2027. A Ruth Asawa retrospective opens October, then Kahlo, Bourgeois, and Peyton.

Tracked sources checked

Katya Kazakina (no new on-thesis column this week), Georgina Adam (Art Market Eye next due Sept 3), Center for Art Law (nothing new; 2026 conference already held May 27), The Gray Market (Tim Schneider on medical leave, reposting archival content — correctly excluded), Provenance Watch (nothing new this week). No new macro/market-economics report since the two already logged. Nothing genuinely new and public on the prospects beat this cycle.
